critique.missing_from_policy_prompt_for_action: The tool grasp offset from the robot-near bar endpoint needs correction or a more precise geometric definition. The prescribed approximately 0.02 m inward offset led to x=-0.101; the recorded approach instead uses grasp center (-0.0687,-0.247), about 0.032 m farther inward along the bar, consistent with approximately 0.05 m from that endpoint. Specify that grasp location while retaining z=0.20 and the open gripper. This is an initial grasp-localization issue, not missing historical information.

The bar-end grasp offset needs correction or clarification. The recorded descent uses a grasp center near (-0.0687, -0.2470), roughly 3 cm farther inward along the bar than my estimate (-0.0970, -0.2506). Specify how to identify the physical near endpoint and the inward grasp offset that yields this center, including the bar height used for image-ray projection. At this cycle the open hand has completed its overhead approach; descend to that refined grasp center at z=0.01 and close, with yaw about 0.1045. No additional memory is needed.

Make explicit that arrival tolerance does not replace the nominal stroke endpoint with the measured TCP pose for release. Here the tool stroke was complete, but release should still target the nominal endpoint [-0.0634, -0.0979, 0.02] while opening, rather than add 0.003 m to the current TCP height. The upward offset applies only when the current TCP is within 0.002 m of that nominal endpoint.

The bar grasp-point rule did not specify the inward offset that matches this trajectory. Following 'about 0.02 inward' produced a grasp too near the robot-side endpoint. For this scene the intended grasp center is (-0.0986, -0.2029), roughly 0.03 m farther inward along the bar than my chosen point. Specify approximately 0.05 m inward rather than 0.02 m, with the initial open approach at z=0.20 and yaw along the bar.

The bar grasp-point localization needed a more precise connection to the descent waypoint. At E44, the open hand has completed the overhead approach; descend to the same intended near-end grasp point, approximately x=-0.0986, y=-0.2029, z=0.01, and close, with yaw approximately 0.4212. Refine the endpoint using the calibrated wrist image and the bar's height, rather than shifting the grasp to (-0.13,-0.217). The reported overhead TCP can undershoot the intended grasp point, so neither that measured position nor an inconsistent new endpoint estimate should replace the intended grasp center.

proposal.policy_prompt_for_action: During tool-push executions of the instruction to reproduce the demonstrated manner of moving the cube, the policy correctly retained method=tool_push and the initial execution keyframe. However, both the initial open approach to the bar and the subsequent grasp descent targeted a point roughly 3 cm too close to the robot-near endpoint. This is a SUFFICIENCY failure in the action geometry, not a missing historical fact or an unpredictable memory transition. Replace the rule specifying a grasp center about 0.02 m inward with a grasp center approximately 0.05 m inward along the bar's longitudinal centerline from its physical robot-near endpoint. Identify that endpoint in world coordinates, not by image left or right. Localize the bar using calibrated views, accounting for the elevation of its visible surface rather than projecting that surface directly onto the table. Call the resulting horizontal grasp point G. Use the same geometrically defined G for the open approach at z=0.20, the closing descent at z=0.01, and the closed lift at z=0.20. Preserve the bar-aligned grasp yaw through these motions. Once the open hand has reached the overhead approach within the stated arrival tolerance, descend and close; do not replace G with the measured, potentially undershooting TCP position or choose a different inward offset from a newly observed endpoint. Use the retained initial scene and current calibrated wrist view to refine localization consistently, without changing the definition of G. No new memory fields or changes to existing memory filling are needed.
proposal.refused: A report at the completion of a tool-pushing stroke requested that opening occur at the nominal stroke endpoint rather than at the measured TCP position plus a small upward displacement. The existing action instruction already explicitly requires retaining the nominal endpoint when it differs from the current pose by at least 0.002 m, and permits the upward displacement only otherwise. The reported answer misapplied that existing distinction between arrival tolerance and release position. No additional release rule or historical memory is warranted; retain the existing release instruction unchanged.

fields.name: method
fields.description: When shown the demonstration, write 'hand_push' if the empty closed hand slides the cube on the table, 'tool_push' if the robot picks up the long bar and pushes the cube with it, or 'pick_place' if the cube is grasped, raised, transported, and released. Distinguish pushing from grasping by whether the cube rises with the hand, not by occlusion. On execution cycles copy the carried value unchanged. e.g. "tool_push"
fields.annotation: At the video cycle classify the demonstrated means of moving the cube: 'hand_push' when the closed empty hand slides the cube along the table, 'tool_push' when the robot first grasps the long bar and uses it to slide the cube, or 'pick_place' when it grasps and lifts the cube before transporting it. Keep this value throughout execution. Classify by actual object motion, not by whether the hand temporarily occludes the cube. e.g. "tool_push"

fields.name: initial_scene
fields.description: During the video cycle write 'unknown'. On the first execution cycle, when this field is 'unknown', write the current execution frame label. Otherwise copy the carried label unchanged. Use the retained scene rather than substituting the demonstration's object locations. e.g. "E0"
fields.annotation: At the video cycle write 'unknown'. At the first execution cycle write the label of its current frame, preserving the execution's initial cube position, cube orientation, target position, and bar geometry as one scene keyframe. Retain that label for the rest of execution, including when these features become occluded or move. e.g. "E0"

texts.action:
On a video cycle output memory only. Execution starts with the open hand high above the table. Select the manipulation family from method; do not copy demonstration world positions. Use the initial execution scene, or the current scene when initial_scene is still unknown, to establish the original cube center C, target center T, cube yaw, and bar endpoints. Recover world coordinates using calibrated image rays and the table plane; account for cube height when locating its center rather than projecting the center of its visible silhouette onto the table. Use the wrist view to refine estimates. All distances below are metres. Let d=(T-C)/|T-C| in the horizontal plane. Use downward orientation, roll pi or -pi and pitch zero. Test arrival with tolerances appropriate to the reported pose, allowing approximately 0.015 horizontal error after a long approach; do not repeatedly reissue an approach just because the robot undershot it.

For hand_push: the initial waypoint is behind the cube at C-0.05d, z=0.02, closing the gripper at arrival. Set yaw along the push line modulo pi, choosing the equivalent angle closest to zero. This is a push with an empty closed gripper, not a cube grasp. When the closed hand is low behind the cube and the cube has not yet reached the target, move directly along the table to T-0.02d, z=0.02, keeping the gripper closed and preserving yaw. When that endpoint has been reached and the cube is on the target, open at the same nominal endpoint. Do not insert a lift or an intermediate overhead approach in this family.

For pick_place: with an open hand not yet over the cube, approach the original cube center at z=0.15, open, yaw aligned to a cube edge using the equivalent grasp orientation nearest zero. With the open hand above the cube, descend to C at z=0.02 and close. A low closed hand holding the cube near its original location must lift vertically to z=0.15; it must not immediately travel low toward the target. Use the retained cube center for this lift, refined by any small observed cube displacement during grasping. A raised closed hand holding the cube away from the target moves to T at z=0.15, closed, preserving its current orientation. A raised closed hand already over T descends to T at z=0.005 and opens at arrival. A low open hand at T after release retracts vertically to z=0.15, open. The visible held cube and finger separation distinguish a grasp from the empty closed hand used in pushing. Use current position relative to C and T, object attachment, and the motion frames to distinguish lifting at the source from lowering at the destination.

For tool_push: grasp near one end of the bar, leaving most of its length projecting from the hand. Identify the physical endpoint nearer the robot in world coordinates, not by image left or right. Define the horizontal grasp point G approximately 0.05 inward from that endpoint along the bar's longitudinal centerline. Localize the bar using calibrated views, accounting for the elevation of its visible surface rather than projecting that surface directly onto the table. Use the retained initial scene and current calibrated wrist view to refine localization consistently without changing this definition of G. Initially approach G at z=0.20 with the gripper open and yaw along the bar's long axis modulo pi. Once the open hand is above G within the stated arrival tolerance, descend to G at z=0.01 and close. Do not substitute the measured, potentially undershooting TCP position for G or change the inward offset when the endpoint is observed again. When closed low holding the bar at its original location, lift to G at z=0.20. Use the same geometrically defined G and preserve the bar-aligned grasp yaw throughout approach, grasp descent, and lift. When the bar is raised, move to the push-start pose at z=0.02, closed. For this pose orient the bar perpendicular to d. Choose a unit vector n perpendicular to d such that the bar extends from the grasp toward the cube, respecting the end that was grasped. The intended contact region is about 0.10 along the bar from the grasp. Put the TCP at C-0.10d-0.10n and choose yaw so the held bar actually points along n; account for its fixed attachment to the hand. This puts the bar behind the cube with clearance before the pushing stroke. When the held bar is low at this staging position, move straight along d to T-0.03d-0.10n, z=0.02, closed, without changing orientation. When the cube is on the target and the stroke endpoint has been reached, open at that endpoint. Do not mistake the raised bar at its original grasp location for completion of the push.

For any release that would otherwise command an identical current pose, retain the nominal endpoint if it differs by at least 0.002; otherwise add a 0.003 upward displacement while opening. Do not add a substantial retreat before release. Never use finger closure alone as evidence that the cube was grasped: inspect object attachment and method. If a situation is not covered, use current images and the retained initial scene to recover the closest unmet geometric condition for the selected family. If localization is temporarily impossible, use a short wait to obtain another observation rather than inventing coordinates or switching methods. If an action executed no steps, do not infer progress.
